in_arabic.name: بطور
in_arabic.meaning: اسم بطور يعني الشخص القوي والشجاع والمستدام

in_urdu.name: بتور
in_urdu.meaning: بتور نام کا مطلب ہے مضبوط، بہادر اور پائیدار

in_pashto.long_meaning: بتور د عربي اصل مذکر نوم دی چی معنی يې د قوي، زړور او دوامداره سړی دے. دا نوم د قرآن کریم د سورة الحجر آیت ٨٨ 'وَلَقَدْ جَعَلْنَا فِي الْأَرْضِ رِزْقًا لَّكُمْ وَمَا أَحْيَيتُمُوهُ' سره تړلی دی، کوم چی د ژوند د دوام او قوت معنی سره نښلوي

historical_references.reference: Ibn Abd al-Hakam, Futuh Misr (The Conquest of Egypt). In this historic account, Batoor is mentioned as the wife of a prominent leader named Ka'ab ibn al-Ashraf in the Arab-Muslim conquest of Egypt (639-641 CE). Ka'ab was a Jewish poet and a chief advisor to the Byzantine governor of Egypt. He had opposed the Muslim invasion and was killed by Muhammad ibn Maslama for his defiance. Batoor was taken as a captive and later ransomed by Caliph Umar.

Ibn Kathir, Al-Bidayah wa-l-Nihayah (The Beginning and the End). In this historical work, Batoor is mentioned as the sister of the Prophet Muhammad's cousin, Ali ibn Abi Talib. She was married to a man named 'Amr ibn Hisham, who was a poet and a leader of the Hawazin tribe in pre-Islamic Arabia. When 'Amr refused to pay the zakat (alms tax) to the Muslims, the Prophet Muhammad led a military campaign against the Hawazin. During the battle, 'Amr was killed, and Batoor and her sisters were taken as captives. They were later released upon the payment of ransom.
